case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] I tell my friends I'm fine, then get irritated when they stop asking.
case-sara.suggestion: You give the fine answer and then feel alone with it; I wonder if you are hoping someone will notice you are not fine.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] I stay late at work after the breakup, because getting home early feels worse.
case-sara.suggestion: Staying late keeps you away from the quiet apartment; maybe going home early brings the aloneness closer.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] I call myself dramatic when I still cry about it, even though I only do it alone.
case-sara.suggestion: Calling yourself dramatic turns the tears into something to hide; I wonder if there is shame about still needing to grieve.

case-sara.text: [Softly] When someone asks how I'm doing, I smile and change the subject.
case-sara.suggestion: You move away quickly with the smile; I wonder if being honestly seen feels both wanted and too exposed.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] When couples post anniversary photos, I roll my eyes and scroll past too fast.
case-sara.suggestion: The eye roll helps you get past it quickly; maybe underneath it there is an ache for that kind of closeness.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] I unfollowed him, then borrowed my friend's phone to check if he looked happier.
case-sara.suggestion: You are trying to stop looking and still need to know; I wonder if part of you is afraid he is relieved you are gone.

case-sara.text: [Softly] I tell myself other people have real problems, so I should be grateful.
case-sara.suggestion: You make your pain smaller before anyone else can; I guess you may be protecting yourself from being dismissed.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] I drafted an apology to him three times this week, even though I do not know what I did wrong.
case-sara.suggestion: The apology gives you something concrete to fix; I wonder if finding fault in yourself feels less helpless than not knowing why he left.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] Nights are the worst; I replay little moments until I find something I could have done differently.
case-sara.suggestion: The replay keeps looking for a handle; maybe blaming yourself gives you a way to feel less powerless with the loss.

case-sara.text: [Softly] When you're kind, I look down and want to change the topic.
case-sara.suggestion: Kindness seems hard to take in directly; maybe it touches a longing you are afraid to show.

case-sara.text: [Dismissive, then quiet] He can keep the photos. I don't need them. I did look to see whether he'd taken ours down, though.
case-sara.suggestion: I wonder if seeing whether the photos are still there is also a way of checking whether you still matter to him.

case-sara.text: [Apologetic] I nearly asked my sister to stay another night. Then I thought she'd already done enough, so I made it sound as though I wanted the flat to myself.
case-sara.suggestion: Maybe it felt risky to let her see you still wanted company, in case that was more than she wanted to give.

case-michael.text: [Firm] If someone questions me in a meeting, I answer fast and louder than I meant to.
case-michael.suggestion: You come in strong before there is time to think; I wonder if the question lands like being exposed as not knowing enough.

case-michael.text: [Defensive] When a coworker corrects me in front of the room, I laugh it off and then feel heat shoot up my neck.
case-michael.suggestion: The laugh covers it fast; I wonder if there is a quick flash of humiliation underneath.

case-michael.text: [Tense] My wife says I am harsh, and I tell her I am just being honest.
case-michael.suggestion: Honesty is the safer position to stand behind; I wonder if softening would bring you closer to guilt.

case-michael.text: [Firm] I keep favors even. I do not like owing anyone.
case-michael.suggestion: You keep the balance carefully; I wonder if owing someone feels like being one-down.

case-michael.text: [Tense and ashamed] When I have to apologize, my jaw tightens and I start explaining the whole situation.
case-michael.suggestion: The explanation comes in quickly; I wonder if apologizing touches shame, almost like losing ground.

case-michael.text: [Tense] I only pour a drink after work because my wife keeps pushing; if she would stop nagging, I would not need it.
case-michael.suggestion: You put the drinking on her pushing; I wonder if the drink also helps you get away from feeling blamed.

case-michael.text: [Firm] I reread everyone's work before a presentation because one mistake would come back on me.
case-michael.suggestion: You are guarding against one mistake landing on you; I wonder if blame feels expected before anything has gone wrong.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] After I blow up, my kid looks careful around me, and I cannot meet his eyes.
case-michael.suggestion: His careful look seems to hit hard; I wonder if it touches shame about being scary to him.

case-michael.text: [Tense] When someone tells me to calm down, it sounds like they are calling me childish.
case-michael.suggestion: That phrase seems to shrink you quickly; I wonder if the anger protects against feeling dismissed.

case-michael.text: [Firm] I do not do feelings; I ask what we are going to do about it.
case-michael.suggestion: You move toward action fast; maybe feelings seem too exposing to stay with for long.

case-michael.text: [Clipped] I could have asked for help with the report. Instead I worked until midnight. I don't want people thinking they have to carry me.
case-michael.suggestion: I wonder if needing help feels close to being seen as not capable enough.

case-michael.text: [Irritated, voice dropping] My son kept asking whether I'd come to his game. I told him I'd already said yes. I've been thinking about his face since then.
case-michael.suggestion: Maybe his asking again hurt because it suggested he wasn't sure he could count on you.

case-jason.text: [Blank] I rehearse every sentence before a meeting, and then my mind still blanks when people turn toward me.
case-jason.suggestion: You prepare carefully, and then the blankness takes over; I wonder if being looked at feels like being evaluated.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] When I get invited out, I say I am busy before I can find out whether I want to go.
case-jason.suggestion: The busy answer comes in fast; I wonder if it protects you from finding out whether you would belong.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] I hear a voice saying 'don't embarrass yourself' before I even open my mouth.
case-jason.suggestion: That warning arrives before you speak; I guess it is trying to protect you from feeling exposed.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] After I speak, I cringe for hours and imagine everyone replaying how ridiculous I sounded.
case-jason.suggestion: The cringe keeps replaying the moment; I wonder if being heard feels close to being laughed at.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] When someone compliments me, I assume they are being polite and missed the awkward part.
case-jason.suggestion: The compliment does not quite get in; I wonder if the awkward part feels more believable than the kind words.

case-jason.text: [Ashamed] Seeing confident people makes me want to disappear, and then I hate myself for envying them.
case-jason.suggestion: Their confidence makes you shrink; maybe the envy is also sadness about feeling outside that world.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] If someone laughs nearby, I assume it is about me and replay what I did wrong.
case-jason.suggestion: You brace for ridicule quickly; I wonder if laughter feels like proof that being visible is dangerous.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] I type a text, read it five times, and delete it before sending.
case-jason.suggestion: You edit yourself right out of contact; I wonder if reaching out feels like giving someone a chance to reject you.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] I drink before events because otherwise I stand by the wall checking my phone.
case-jason.suggestion: The drink helps you leave the wall; I wonder if it shields you from feeling exposed.

case-jason.text: [Ashamed] I stay quiet even when I have a good idea, and then replay it all day.
case-jason.suggestion: You stay hidden and then keep replaying it; maybe speaking up feels risky, but staying silent brings shame.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] I tell people I'm busy when they invite me. Then I check whether they went without me. I know that doesn't make much sense.
case-jason.suggestion: Maybe you want to be included, and saying you're busy protects you from finding out what it would be like to join them.

case-jason.text: [Quiet] I didn't tell my friend I'd had a bad day. I asked about his instead. I kept hoping he'd notice I wasn't saying much.
case-jason.suggestion: I wonder if you wanted him to notice you needed care without having to risk asking for it.

case-laura.text: [Flat and guarded] When someone is kind, I get suspicious fast, like warmth always has a catch.
case-laura.suggestion: You distance from kindness; I wonder if closeness can stir an old fear that warmth will turn into danger or betrayal.

case-laura.text: [Fearful] When voices rise, I freeze before I know whether the anger is even aimed at me.
case-laura.suggestion: The freeze arrives before the facts; maybe some part of you learned that fear had to move faster than thought.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] Part of me feels guilty that I seem numb when people expect me to be grateful.
case-laura.suggestion: You judge the numbness; I guess it may be protecting a very sore grief that gratitude cannot reach.

case-laura.text: [Flat and guarded] I avoid movies with family fights because the sound follows me home.
case-laura.suggestion: You steer clear; I wonder if the sound might wake old terror and shame that do not stay on the screen.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] Sometimes I stare at the wall until the room goes flat and nothing can reach me.
case-laura.suggestion: The flatness seems protective; I wonder if it keeps you away from the ache that might come if the room felt real.

case-laura.text: [Tense and guarded] A kind man asked me out, and I immediately listed every reason he would probably hurt me.
case-laura.suggestion: The list comes in fast; I wonder if wanting closeness and expecting betrayal arrive almost together.

case-laura.text: [Ashamed] When someone touches my shoulder, I flinch before I know them, then feel ashamed.
case-laura.suggestion: The flinch comes before recognition; I wonder if touch may carry danger so quickly, and then shame comes for needing that protection.

case-laura.text: [Distant] When people say trauma survivors are strong, I want to leave the room.
case-laura.suggestion: That praise pushes you away; I wonder if it misses the shame and aloneness that still feel hard to reach.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] My routine is work, groceries, home. It feels safer that way.
case-laura.suggestion: You keep the world narrow and predictable; I wonder if smallness helps control risk and keep old pain from getting too close.

case-laura.text: [Tense and ashamed] If I cry, I apologize before anyone even reacts.
case-laura.suggestion: The apology comes before anyone has done anything; I wonder if tears carry an old expectation of danger, blame, or care that was not safe.

case-laura.text: [Guarded] When my friend offers to come over, I say I'm working. I wasn't working last night. I did keep looking at my phone.
case-laura.suggestion: Maybe keeping her outside protects you, while another part of you still hopes she will make contact.

case-laura.text: [Flat, looking away] I don't mind that he returned the key. That's settled. I haven't taken his name out of my contacts yet, though.
case-laura.suggestion: I wonder if removing his name would make the ending feel more final than you're ready for right now.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] A disrespectful tone flips a switch in me before I know what got hit.
case-carlos.suggestion: It flips you fast; I wonder if under the heat is a flash of humiliation before anger takes over.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] If I back down, it sits in my chest for days.
case-carlos.suggestion: It stays with you for days; I wonder if backing down might touch something more than the argument, like feeling small or taken over.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] When someone tells me what to do, my first thought is, 'Who do you think you are?'
case-carlos.suggestion: That question comes up fast; I guess being directed can feel like being put underneath someone else's power.

case-carlos.text: [Ashamed] My son saw me slam a door, and later I could not stop seeing his face.
case-carlos.suggestion: I wonder if his face brought up not just regret, but shame and fear about what he is learning from you.

case-carlos.text: [Tense] After a fight, my wife gets quiet, and I cannot look at her face.
case-carlos.suggestion: Her quiet seems to reach past the anger; I wonder if looking at her would bring up regret, tenderness, and the fear that you scared her.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] I puff up when someone challenges me, before they can see it lands.
case-carlos.suggestion: You armor up fast; I wonder if it covers that split second where the challenge actually lands and makes you feel less-than.

case-carlos.text: [Ashamed] I break things so I do not hit people, but afterward I can see everyone is still scared.
case-carlos.suggestion: You are trying not to hit people; I wonder if breaking things pushes hurt away for a moment, then leaves shame when you see the fear.

case-carlos.text: [Defensive] My father used to say feelings make men weak, and I still hear that in my head.
case-carlos.suggestion: That rule is still loud; I wonder if it is guarding against the risk of feeling tender, exposed, or powerless.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] I replay disrespect for days, planning how I should have won it in the moment.
case-carlos.suggestion: You keep trying to win it afterward; I wonder if the replay helps hold back the humiliation of feeling small right then.

case-carlos.text: [Fearful] I want to do better for my family, and then I hear myself sounding like the men I hated.
case-carlos.suggestion: I wonder if under the determination there is fear and grief about becoming someone your family has to brace around.

case-carlos.text: [Defensive] The crew can joke about me. I joke about them. But when the new lad joined in, I had to put him straight.
case-carlos.suggestion: Could there be a worry that letting his joke pass would mean losing respect in front of the others?

case-carlos.text: [Tense, then quiet] My daughter asked her uncle to help instead of me. I said fine. Then I found a reason to go out before he arrived.
case-carlos.suggestion: Maybe it hurt to see her turn to someone else, and leaving kept you from having to show that hurt.

case-nina.text: [Guilty] Resting makes me feel selfish, even when I am so tired I can barely stand.
case-nina.suggestion: Rest stirs guilt; I wonder if part of you came to feel that love was safer when you kept earning your place.

case-nina.text: [Apologetic] I say yes and then resent it, but I still cannot stop.
case-nina.suggestion: You say yes and anger follows; maybe the resentment is pointing to needs that still feel too risky to claim.

case-nina.text: [Torn] When I ask for help, I apologize before they can look annoyed.
case-nina.suggestion: You apologize before anyone reacts; I guess there is a fear that needing help will cost you acceptance.

case-nina.text: [Guilty] If the house is messy when people stop by, I start explaining before they say anything.
case-nina.suggestion: You explain before there is even a charge; I wonder if the mess might touch shame about having to prove you are good through doing.

case-nina.text: [Apologetic] If someone seems disappointed, I start fixing things before I know what I want.
case-nina.suggestion: The fixing comes in fast; I wonder if disappointment might touch an old fear that love could be withdrawn.

case-nina.text: [Torn] I swallow my anger because it is not nice, and then I resent everyone quietly.
case-nina.suggestion: You swallow the anger to stay kind; maybe a younger part learned that having needs would threaten love.

case-nina.text: [Tired] I take care of everyone, and when nobody notices, I get sharp with myself for caring.
case-nina.suggestion: You turn on the wish quickly; I wonder if there is a lonely longing to be cared for without having to earn it.

case-nina.text: [Apologetic] I try to say no and then add three explanations before they answer.
case-nina.suggestion: The explanations rush in after the no; I wonder if a part of you is trying to keep acceptance safe.

case-nina.text: [Torn] I tell myself others have it worse, and then I keep going.
case-nina.suggestion: You make your needs smaller and move on; I wonder if staying acceptable has meant not taking up much room.

case-nina.text: [Tired] If I slow down after everyone is asleep, a lump rises in my throat.
case-nina.suggestion: The lump comes when no one needs you; maybe grief is close and asking to be noticed.

case-nina.text: [Smiling] They said I didn't need to bring anything. I cooked anyway. Arriving empty-handed would have felt strange.
case-nina.suggestion: I wonder if bringing something helps you feel sure there's a place for you there.

case-nina.text: [Apologetic] I tell everyone I'm happy to organise it. Then I get cross when nobody offers to help. They can't read my mind, so I suppose it's my fault.
case-nina.suggestion: Maybe asking directly feels risky, as if needing help could change how they see you.

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] If you glance at the clock, my stomach drops like you are already leaving me.
case-aisha.suggestion: That glance becomes a leaving signal; I wonder if underneath the drop is a fear that you stop mattering once someone turns away.

case-aisha.text: [Furious] When he did not text back, I went from quiet to furious before I knew what happened.
case-aisha.suggestion: You swing fast; maybe the fury rushes in to protect the scared, raw part that feels left.

case-aisha.text: [Numb] Sometimes I want to scratch my arms just to cut through the numbness.
case-aisha.suggestion: You want a way through the numbness; I wonder if there is unbearable emptiness underneath.

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] I scared everyone last week saying I might kill myself, but he texted today, so it is fine and maybe I do not need to talk about it.
case-aisha.suggestion: Part of you wants to close it quickly now that contact came back; I wonder if looking back at how close the edge got feels frightening.

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] If you cancel, a part of me wants to never come back and pretend I do not care.
case-aisha.suggestion: That cancellation stings like being dropped; I wonder if rejecting first feels safer than waiting for it to happen again.

case-aisha.text: [Ashamed] When I ask someone to stay, I hate how intense I sound afterward.
case-aisha.suggestion: You hate the intensity right where you need closeness; maybe shame says your need is too much.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] Kindness makes me sob, and then I want to bolt from the room.
case-aisha.suggestion: It lands big; I guess one part longs for the kindness and another expects needing it to become dangerous.

case-aisha.text: [Ashamed] I test people to find out if they really care, then hate how needy it sounds.
case-aisha.suggestion: You test and then feel ashamed; I wonder if you are trying to prove you matter before risking trust.

case-aisha.text: [Ashamed] After I lash out, I call myself disgusting before anyone else can say it.
case-aisha.suggestion: The attack turns inward quickly; I wonder if calling yourself disgusting gets there before the fear that someone else will.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] I panic when I say goodbye, even when I know you'll be back.
case-aisha.suggestion: Goodbyes spike panic even when your mind knows better; I wonder if they touch that old fear that no one comes back.

case-aisha.text: [Sharp, then watching] Don't bother saying you'll remember me next week. You'll say it because you have to. I keep wondering whether you've thought about me between sessions, though.
case-aisha.suggestion: I wonder if wanting to matter to me between sessions also makes you wary of an answer that might disappoint you.

case-aisha.text: [Defiant, voice unsteady] I said I didn't need the friendship anymore. Deleted her number. I still know it by heart, so that didn't really do anything.
case-aisha.suggestion: Maybe saying you didn't need her was a way to get ahead of the fear that she might not need you.

case-david.text: [Hopeless] When my wife calls me cold, I make a cutting joke before she can see it hurt.
case-david.suggestion: The joke gets there first; I wonder if it guards against a sting of being seen as failing or not enough.

case-david.text: [Dismissive] I do not like being told what to do; it makes me feel like someone has the upper hand.
case-david.suggestion: You resist direction; I wonder if it lands like someone has made you small.

case-david.text: [Dismissive] If I cannot be the best, why bother trying at all?
case-david.suggestion: You aim for the top; I wonder if ordinary can feel almost like disappearing.

case-david.text: [Distant] I plan big gestures, people react well, and then I feel empty afterward.
case-david.suggestion: I wonder if after the gesture lands, a lonely place still asks whether they want you or only what you can provide.

case-david.text: [Dismissive] Apologizing makes me cringe; I start explaining before the words are even out.
case-david.suggestion: It feels humiliating; I wonder if admitting wrong might touch an old shame of being reduced to failure.

case-david.text: [Avoidant] In hard talks, I reach for my phone when the conversation starts to get personal.
case-david.suggestion: You reach for an exit as closeness comes in; maybe being personal feels dangerous when you expect judgment.

case-david.text: [Controlled] I brag when I feel insecure, before anyone can see the gap.
case-david.suggestion: You pump yourself up quickly; I guess it covers the fragile gap before anyone else can see it.

case-david.text: [Wounded but sharp] If the kids push back, I hear disrespect and go straight into lecture mode.
case-david.suggestion: Their pushback seems to hit your authority fast; I wonder if the lecture covers a flash of shame.

case-david.text: [Wounded but sharp] When my wife misunderstands me, I get sharp and keep proving my point.
case-david.suggestion: You keep proving the point; I wonder if beneath the anger there is grief about not being known.

case-david.text: [Controlled] If my wife stays, I feel trapped and criticized; if she leaves, I feel humiliated. There is no winning.
case-david.suggestion: Both options threaten you; I wonder if each one touches the same fear of being seen as not enough.

case-david.text: [Coolly] I didn't attend the farewell dinner. It wasn't important. I did notice that nobody contacted me afterwards to ask why.
case-david.suggestion: I wonder if not being asked touched a wish to be missed, even while you were telling yourself the dinner didn't matter.

case-david.text: [Controlled] I don't need my wife's approval. But when she thanks the neighbour for helping, I find myself listing everything I've done that week.
case-david.suggestion: Perhaps her thanks to him stir a fear that what you offer is no longer enough to matter to her.

case-marcus.text: [Slow and flat] Most days I feel shut down. People talk, and I mostly just nod.
case-marcus.suggestion: You feel sealed off; I wonder if numbness may be keeping a lot of pain from getting through all at once.

case-marcus.text: [Low voice] I sleep with the TV on so the room does not get too quiet.
case-marcus.suggestion: You drown out the quiet; maybe silence brings memories and grief too close.

case-marcus.text: [Quiet and guarded] I pick the seat where I can see the door, and I get tense if someone stands behind me.
case-marcus.suggestion: The seat choice seems to organize safety; I wonder if part of you is still expecting the room to turn dangerous.

case-marcus.text: [Low voice] I do not answer when my sister calls, even though I know she is just checking in.
case-marcus.suggestion: You keep distance; I wonder if her voice gets through the numbness and makes feelings harder to manage.

case-marcus.text: [Tense] Loud noises make me jump and then I get angry at myself.
case-marcus.suggestion: You jump then judge; I wonder if the anger covers shame about being vulnerable.

case-marcus.text: [Quiet and guarded] When good things happen, I notice myself waiting for the other shoe to drop.
case-marcus.suggestion: The good stays at a distance; maybe letting it matter makes loss feel too close.

case-marcus.text: [Flat] I drink to knock myself out sometimes because I do not want to dream.
case-marcus.suggestion: You knock yourself out before sleep can pull you back there; I guess it keeps nightmares and feelings at bay.

case-marcus.text: [Slow and flat] I keep the lights low at home so nothing feels too sharp.
case-marcus.suggestion: You keep things dim and softened; I wonder if brightness feels too exposing or too sharp.

case-marcus.text: [Quiet and guarded] I do not remember the last time I laughed, and even trying feels fake.
case-marcus.suggestion: You cannot reach laughter; I wonder if joy feels wrong somehow after so much loss.

case-marcus.text: [Flat] I tell myself I am better off alone. Closeness gets complicated fast.
case-marcus.suggestion: That part seems protective; I wonder if it fears that closeness means hurting someone, being hurt, or losing control again.

case-marcus.text: [Flat] I put the neighbour's invitation in the bin. Took it out again. Haven't replied.
case-marcus.suggestion: Maybe there is some wish for company there, alongside the need to keep your distance.

case-marcus.text: [Guarded] I don't ask people to remember the date. Still notice when nobody does. Doesn't make much sense.
case-marcus.suggestion: I wonder if you want the loss to matter to someone else too, without having to explain it all.
